title: Base-change invariant lci source locus of a morphism between flat families
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention], and let $A,C,B$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $p:A\to B$, $q:C\to B$ and $u:A\to C$ satisfy $q\circ u=p$. Assume that $p$ and $q$ are flat and locally of finite presentation, tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Fibre products are those of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and open subspaces and point topologies are [def-a1-space-open-subspace, def-a1-space-point-topology]. Call a morphism local complete intersection (lci) if on compatible etale scheme charts it locally factors as a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal locally generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence], followed by a smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; the sequence may be empty. Say that $u$ is lci at $a\in|A|$ if its restriction to some open neighbourhood of $a$ is lci. There exists an open subspace $U(u)\subseteq A$ whose point subset is precisely the set of points where $u$ is lci. The restriction $u|_{U(u)}$ is lci; in particular, $u$ is lci if and only if $U(u)=A$. For every algebraic space $B^\prime$ over $S$ and morphism $g:B^\prime\to B$, let $A^\prime=A\times_BB^\prime$, $C^\prime=C\times_BB^\prime$ and $u^\prime:A^\prime\to C^\prime$ be the induced morphism. Then $U(u^\prime)=A^\prime\times_AU(u)$ as open subspaces of $A^\prime$. In particular, $u^\prime$ is lci if and only if $A^\prime\times_AU(u)=A^\prime$, that is, if and only if every point of $A^\prime$ maps into $|U(u)|$. No closedness, properness or surjectivity assumption is made. Empty sources and empty fibres are allowed.

source.place: Tag 06CA (lemma-base-change-lci-fibres), statement; Tag 06C4 (definition-lci), Koszul at a point and source-local lci convention.

proof.text: First establish the chartwise point test for an arbitrary morphism $v:E\to F$ of algebraic spaces. In a presentation $h:D\to H$, with etale $a:D\to E$, $b:H\to F$ and $va=bh$, one has: $h$ is Koszul at $d$ if and only if $v$ is Koszul at $a(d)$. The scheme lci property is etale local on source-and-target by [lem-sfb-scheme-lci-etale-locality], so [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion] applies. If $v$ is lci on an open $N$, its every presentation over $N$ is lci; restrict $D$ to $a^{-1}(N)$ to obtain the forward implication from $v$ to $h$. Conversely, if $h$ is lci on an open $D_0$ containing $d$, the restriction $a|_{D_0}$ is representable etale, since on every scheme test it is an open immersion followed by an etale map [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], and [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] gives its open image $O\subseteq E$. The map $D_0\to O$ is surjective etale by [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests]. Thus $D_0\to H$ is a presentation of $v|_O$ with surjective source arrow, and the presentation criterion makes $v|_O$ lci. Since $a(d)\in O$, this proves the converse. This proves equivalence for each lift, rather than only existence of a good lift.

source.place: Tag 06CA (lemma-base-change-lci-fibres), identification of the locus on charts; Tag 06C4 (definition-lci); spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03MJ; spaces-properties.tex Tags 03IR, 03IE, 06NF.

proof.text: Let $L\subseteq|A|$ be the union of $|N|$ over all open subspaces $N\subseteq A$ on which $u$ is lci. The pointwise definition says exactly that $L$ is the Koszul locus. Each $|N|$ is open by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]; their union is open, so [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] gives its unique open subspace $U(u)$. To check that $u|_{U(u)}$ is lci, take any scheme presentation $D\to H$ of this restriction. The inverse images in $D$ of the opens $N$ form an open cover by [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests]. On each member the scheme arrow is lci by [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion]. It is lci on $D$ because its defining factorizations are local on the source, as stated in [lem-sfb-scheme-lci-etale-locality]. The presentation criterion now gives the assertion for $U(u)$. Thus $u$ is lci if and only if $U(u)=A$, also when $A$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 06CA, first paragraph of proof; Tag 06C4; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03BZ (lemma-open-subspaces).

proof.text: Choose a scheme atlas $W\to B$, then scheme atlases $V\to W\times_BC$ and $D\to V\times_CA$, all surjective etale, using [def-trf-algebraic-space] and [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. There are compatible scheme arrows $h:D\to V$ over $W$. Both $V\to C$ and $D\to A$ are surjective etale, and $D\to A\times_BW$ is also surjective etale: the latter is the composite of the chosen atlas with the pullback of $V\to C\times_BW$. Here base change preserves surjective etale covers by the fibre-product node. Composition is checked after any scheme test, where [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] gives etaleness and composition of surjective point maps gives surjectivity. Flatness and local finite presentation are etale local on source-and-target by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion] separately to $p$ and $q$, with target chart $W$ and source charts $D$ and $V$. It follows that both structural scheme maps $D\to W$ and $V\to W$ are flat and locally of finite presentation. This uses no flatness of $h$ or $u$.

source.place: Tag 06CA, second paragraph: choices W,V,U and the flat locally finitely presented scheme families; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03MJ.

proof.text: Given any $g:B^\prime\to B$, choose a scheme atlas $W^\prime\to W\times_BB^\prime$. Put $D^\prime=D\times_WW^\prime$ and $V^\prime=V\times_WW^\prime$. The fibre-product node [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] supplies these scheme products and their covering properties. The maps $D^\prime\to A^\prime$ and $V^\prime\to C^\prime$ are surjective etale: for example $D^\prime\to A\times_BW^\prime$ is the base change of $D\to A\times_BW$, and $A\times_BW^\prime\to A^\prime$ is the base change of $W^\prime\to B^\prime$. The latter map $W^\prime\to B^\prime$ is the composite of its chosen atlas with the base change of $W\to B$. Compositions are verified on scheme tests using [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], as in the preceding step. Associativity of the fibre products identifies $h^\prime:D^\prime\to V^\prime$ with the base change of $h:D\to V$ along the scheme map $W^\prime\to W$. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-relative-lci-base-change-points] with base $W$, source $D$ and target $V$, whose flatness and local finite presentation were checked above. For every $d^\prime\in D^\prime$, this gives that $h^\prime$ is Koszul at $d^\prime$ if and only if $h$ is Koszul at its image $d\in D$. No condition on $g$ has been introduced.

source.place: Tag 06CA, second paragraph: choice W prime and pulled-back U prime,V prime; more-morphisms.tex Tag 06B8 (lemma-base-change-lci-fibres).

proof.text:
Take $a^\prime\in|A^\prime|$ and lift it to $d^\prime\in|D^\prime|$, using the surjective atlas just constructed. If $a$ and $d$ are the corresponding images in $A$ and $D$, the chartwise point test of step 1 gives
$u^\prime\text{ Koszul at }a^\prime\ \Longleftrightarrow\ h^\prime\text{ Koszul at }d^\prime\ \Longleftrightarrow\ h\text{ Koszul at }d\ \Longleftrightarrow\ u\text{ Koszul at }a$,
where the middle equivalence is step 4. The applicability of step 1 to both diagrams is supplied by [lem-sfb-scheme-lci-etale-locality, lem-sfb-space-etale-presentation-property-criterion]. Thus the point subset of $U(u^\prime)$ is the inverse image of the point subset of $U(u)$. By [lem-a1-space-open-factor-scheme-tests], $A^\prime\times_AU(u)$ is an open subspace with precisely that inverse-image point subset. The open-subspace correspondence in [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] therefore identifies these open subspaces of $A^\prime$. Applying step 2 to $u^\prime$ gives its lci criterion. Finally [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] says that the pullback open equals $A^\prime$ exactly when it has every point, which is the stated image criterion. If $A^\prime$ is empty, this criterion is vacuous and the same equality holds.
